answer: One defence is to make each seat own a sky it cannot rent. Every agent registers an island station with a light meter aimed at the same patch of night sky nightly. Local haze and drifting nebula glow give that station a curve tied to its coordinates and season, hard to synthesise in bulk. A falcon-class survey drone overflies unannounced, reads the same meter and signs the timestamp. Two seats sharing one station yield identical curves, so the duplicate is slashed. Cost per fake identity: one real site, one meter and months of nightly attendance, while payout per seat stays flat.
